title: Why building eval platforms is hard — Phil Hetzel, Braintrust
talk_summary: Phil Hetzel of Braintrust argues that eval platforms are a systems problem, not a UI problem: the real difficulty is the data layer for large, semi-structured agent traces plus a flywheel connecting production observability back into offline evals. He sketches maturity stages from spreadsheet+for-loop to playground-style experimentation to production tracing, and notes headless/agent-driven eval use cases.

takeaways.technique: Failure-mode-driven scoring functions from production traces
takeaways.what_they_do: They derive scoring functions from observed failure modes in real production trace data rather than inventing generic rubrics, then run those scorers offline and online.
Pipe real production traffic into a store, analyze it, pull representative examples back into an offline eval set, improve, and repeat for the agent's lifetime.

takeaways.technique: Treat traces as large semi-structured blobs, not rows
takeaways.what_they_do: They warn that agent spans are 10-20MB of unstructured text and that cramming them into Postgres rows causes performance problems; they split low-latency ingest from aggregate analytics and use object storage for large payloads.
takeaways.numbers: spans 10-20 MB vs traditional couple of kilobytes

takeaways.what_they_do: They design the eval data layer so a coding agent (Codex/Claude Code) can pull aggregate eval data via plain SQL and act on it, since many users never touch the UI.

takeaways.technique: Automatic tracing via a central AI gateway
takeaways.what_they_do: They suggest adding tracing automatically at an AI proxy/gateway so callers have no choice but to be traced, giving central governance.

takeaways.technique: Topic modeling to surface unknown unknowns
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of making humans read all traces, they cluster/topic-model production data to tell you how the agent is actually being used and where to spend engineering time.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Don't make me look across a whole bunch of traces. Just tell me how people are are using our our agent
